commitResults.messageTitle: Person class: Persist created, edited and viewed times
commitResults.messageBody:
Contacts have no record of when they were added, changed or looked at,
so later features (sort by activity, follow-ups) have nothing to build
on.

Let's,
* add an immutable Activity class holding optional created, last edited
  and last viewed times
* give Person an Activity, a withActivity copy method and a
  hasSameDetails comparison that ignores activity
* save the times as optional ISO-8601 UTC strings in the JSON file, and
  load a missing time as absent so v1.3 files still load
* keep activity when edit and tag replace a person
* describe the stored format in the Developer Guide

Optional times keep unknown history absent instead of inventing dates.

commitResults.messageTitle: Model: Record contact add, edit and view activity
commitResults.messageBody:
Activity fields exist on Person but nothing sets them, so every time
stays absent.

Let's,
* give ModelManager a Clock and a now() that returns whole seconds
* add Model#editPerson as the single rule for last edited: it does
  nothing when the details are unchanged, and otherwise stores the new
  person with the target's activity and last edited set to now
* add Model#viewPerson to set last viewed and the viewed person
* record created time in AddCommand, and use editPerson in EditCommand
  and TagCommand and viewPerson in ViewCommand
* document the rule in the Developer Guide with a sequence diagram, and
  note in the User Guide that view records the last viewed time

Putting the rule in the model lets later commands (notes, star,
follow-up, photo) record edits without repeating the timestamp logic.

commitResults.messageTitle: Activity: Match the agreed storage contract
commitResults.messageBody:
The agreed v1.4 specification asks for whole-second UTC times and an
error that names the bad field. The first version accepted fractions of
a second and offsets, and reported every bad time with one message.

Let's,
* accept only times written as 2026-10-17T04:12:33Z, and reject
  fractions, offsets, spaces, empty text, 24:00:00 and leap seconds
* report a bad time as Invalid contact data: '<field>' must be an
  ISO-8601 UTC timestamp., naming createdAt, lastEditedAt or
  lastViewedAt, and share the message pattern for later fields
* keep Activity times to whole seconds
* document on the Person constructors that existing contacts are copied
  with withActivity or the model edit operation
* update the Developer Guide

commitResults.messageTitle: Person class: Add toBuilder and use Singapore time
commitResults.messageBody:
The agreed v1.4 specification asks #105 to own one copy API that keeps
every field, so later features do not rebuild a contact with an
incomplete constructor call and lose data. It also fixes display and
"today" to Asia/Singapore.

Let's,
* add Person#toBuilder and a Person.Builder seeded with every field,
  and make withActivity use it
* copy contacts with toBuilder in the edit and tag commands
* default the model clock to Asia/Singapore through
  Model.DISPLAY_ZONE
* use a local variable for the created-time copy in AddCommand and
  point setViewedPerson users to viewPerson
* describe both in the Developer Guide and document the activity time
  fields in the User Guide data file section

commitResults.messageTitle: LogicManager: Undo a command whose save failed
commitResults.messageBody:
The agreed specification says a failed save must leave the data as it
was. LogicManager ran the command and then saved, so a failed save left
the change (and its time stamp) in memory.

Let's,
* add Model#createSnapshot and Model#restore, with an opaque Snapshot of
  the contacts, the viewed contact and the visible-list filter
* take a snapshot before each command and restore it when saving fails,
  for both IO and permission errors
* show the created, last edited and last viewed times in the detail
  panel in Singapore time, with an em dash for unknown times
* document both in the Developer and User Guides

Undo history can extend the same snapshot later.

commitResults.messageTitle: JsonAdaptedPerson: Name the field for non-string times
commitResults.messageBody:
A createdAt, lastEditedAt or lastViewedAt value that is a JSON object,
array, number or boolean made Jackson fail while reading the file, so
the user got a generic error instead of the agreed field-specific one.

Let's,
* read the three times as Object and let parseTime reject anything
  that is not a string with the field-specific message
* add a JSON-level test for all three fields

This way the data file error always names the field that is wrong.

commitResults.messageTitle: ModelManager: Check the target on a no-op edit
commitResults.messageBody:
editPerson returned early when the new details matched the target, so
a missing or stale target was accepted silently, although the Model
API says the target must exist and a real edit throws for it.

Let's,
* throw PersonNotFoundException before the no-op return when the
  target is not in the address book
* add a test for a no-op edit of a missing target

This way a no-op edit follows the same contract as any other edit.

The detail panel put its fields and the new CREATED, LAST EDITED and
LAST VIEWED rows in a VBox with no scrolling, so the bottom rows could
not be reached when the panel was short or the content grew. The #103
agreement requires a vertically scrolling detail panel.

Let's,
* wrap the details in a ScrollPane that fits the width and never shows
  a horizontal bar
* look inside the ScrollPane in the panel and main window tests, since
  lookup does not reach its content before it has a skin
* add a test for the scrolling settings

This way every row stays reachable at any window height.

commitResults.messageTitle: PersonDetailPanel: Keep the scroll area dark
commitResults.messageBody:
Wrapping the details in a ScrollPane made the panel white, because a
ScrollPane and its viewport have a light default background. The light
detail text became almost unreadable. Unit tests cannot see this; it
showed up when the app was run.

Let's,
* give the ScrollPane a detail-scroll style class
* make it and its viewport transparent in DarkTheme.css, and drop the
  inline style that only covered the ScrollPane itself

This way the panel keeps the dark theme and the text stays readable.

commitResults.messageTitle: Developer Guide: Refine target user and value proposition
commitResults.messageBody:
The target user profile and value proposition do not yet mention
that users find saving contacts on a phone too much effort during an
event, forget many contacts afterwards, or may have unreliable
internet at crowded venues.

Add these points so that the profile matches the persona and the
user stories, and rewrite the value proposition to lead with the
outcome and mention that data is stored locally.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add view command to show a person's details
commitResults.messageBody:
Users can only see a compact summary of each person in the list,
and there is no command to look at a single person on its own.

Add the view command, which takes the index of a person in the
displayed list and shows that person's details in the result
display. An invalid index is rejected in the same way as for the
delete command. The detail panel will be added in a later change.
Add view command

The view command reports a generic format error when the user gives
more than one index or an index larger than the integer limit, and
reports an invalid index when the person list is empty. The delete
command already reports each of these cases specifically.

Show the same specific messages as the delete command for multiple
indexes and for an oversized index, and show that the person list is
empty when there is nobody to view.
Handle view command edge cases

commitResults.messageTitle: Add detail panel for the view command
commitResults.messageBody:
The view command shows the viewed person as a single line of text in
the result display.

This is hard to read when a person has many tags, and it disappears as
soon as the next command is run.

Let's add a detail panel next to the person list that shows the name,
phone, email, LinkedIn handle and tags of the viewed person, and shows
that no contact is selected until a person is viewed.

The model keeps track of the viewed person so that the panel can follow
it without the UI having to know about the view command. The minimum
window width is raised from 450 to 700 to fit the panel.

commitResults.messageBody:

not exercised by any test.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add MainWindow test for the detail panel
commitResults.messageBody:
The code that adds the detail panel to the main window is not
exercised by any test, so a mistake in how the panel is wired up

Add detail panel for the view command

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep detail panel in sync with the contact list
commitResults.messageBody:
The detail panel keeps showing the viewed person after that person
has been edited, tagged or deleted, or after the address book has been
cleared, so it can show details that are out of date or no longer exist.

Let's make the model update the viewed person whenever it replaces or
removes that person, and clear it when all data is replaced, so the
panel shows the updated contact or goes back to showing that no contact
is selected.

The default window is 740 by 600, which is too small now that the
main window shows the person list and the detail panel side by side.

Change the default to 900 by 720, so that the person list keeps its
width and the detail panel has room for the details of a contact.

commitResults.messageTitle: User Guide: Add view command section
commitResults.messageBody:
The user guide does not describe the view command or the detail panel
that it fills, so users cannot find out how to see all the details of

Add a section for view with its format, what the detail panel shows,
examples and the error messages, together with a screenshot of the
panel, and add view to the command summary.

commitResults.messageTitle: Note class: Add optional note to contacts
commitResults.messageBody:
Contacts have no place for free-form remarks, such as where the
person was met or what to follow up on.

Let's add an optional Note of at most 1000 characters to Person and
carry it through Person.Builder, so that copies made with toBuilder keep
it. The note is saved as a note string in the data file. A missing note
loads as no note, so older files still load, and a blank, too long or
non-string note makes the file invalid with a message naming the field.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add note command to set and clear a note
commitResults.messageBody:
Users cannot change the note of a contact once the Note field exists.

Add note INDEX nt/TEXT to set or replace a note and note INDEX clear to
remove it. Blank and too long notes are rejected with their own
messages. Setting the same note again, or clearing a missing note,
changes nothing and does not update the last edited time. The command
copies the contact with toBuilder and Model#editPerson, so the other
details and the activity times are kept.

commitResults.messageTitle: Detail panel: Show the note and scroll
commitResults.messageBody:
The detail panel does not show the note of a contact, and it cannot
show more than fits on the screen.

Let's show the full note below the tags, wrapped to the width of the
panel, and put the details in a scroll pane that scrolls vertically
only, so that a long note can be read without a second scroll bar or
text running off the side.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

The User Guide and Developer Guide do not describe notes.

Add the note command, its error messages and the note field of the data
file to the User Guide, and describe the Note field and its storage in
the Developer Guide.

The note command parser parses the index in two separate return
statements, one of which is longer than the line limit.

Work out which form was typed first, reject the other shapes with the
format error, then parse the index once and build the command in one
place. The order of the errors stays the same: a wrong shape is still
reported before a bad index, which a new test checks.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep note text out of the logs and storage
commitResults.messageBody:
The text of a note is personal, but it could be written to the log
through the logged command, through Person.toString when the address
book is logged at startup, and through the error log of the main window.
The data file also accepted an empty note, which the User Guide says is
invalid.

Hide the arguments of a note command wherever a command is logged, and
show only the length of a note in toString. Reject an empty note string
in the data file, because a person without a note is saved as null.
Add tests that capture the log output and check the note text is not in
it.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test the log of a failed command in the window
commitResults.messageBody:
The main window logs a command when it fails, but no test makes a
command fail through the window, so that line never runs in the tests
and it is not checked that a note command is logged without its text.

Add a test that fails a note command through the command box and checks
that the log has the hidden command and not the text of the note.

commitResults.messageTitle: Tag class: Enforce canonical tag validation
commitResults.messageBody:
Tags accept only alphanumeric characters and preserve input casing,
with no maximum length.

The tagging MVP requires hyphens and plus signs, a 1 to 20 character
limit, and case-insensitive behavior.

Let's enforce the validation rules, normalize tags to lowercase, and add
tests covering the required behavior.
Tag class: Enforce canonical tag validation

Support adding one or more tags to a person while preserving
their existing tags, with parser and command test coverage.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge team master into tag command branch
commitResults.messageBody:
The tag command branch needs the team's v1.3 changes to resolve PR
conflicts. Bring in the view command, detail panel, LinkedIn support,
and address removal. Preserve both tag and view parsing, and update
tagging and its tests to retain LinkedIn details.

Adding an existing tag replaces the person needlessly, and an
oversized index produces a generic format error. Keep duplicate tags
as a no-op, report index overflow consistently with delete and view,
and test filtered-list targeting, equality, and hash codes.
Add tag command

Tag commands give inconsistent feedback for invalid person indexes, and
several input edge cases lack focused test coverage.

Report the person-index error for zero, negative, non-numeric, and
out-of-range indexes. Add parser and command tests for missing or invalid
tags and case-insensitive duplicates, while preserving the usage message
when the tag parameter is missing.

commitResults.messageTitle: Align index errors across person commands
commitResults.messageBody:
Delete and view report different errors from tag for invalid person
indexes. The duplicate-tag command test also depends on the parser.

Use the same person-index error across all three commands while keeping
usage feedback for missing indexes. Construct the duplicate-tag command
directly so its test covers command behavior independently.
Handle tag command edge cases

following the v1.3 release.

Document tag syntax, validation, additive updates, and duplicate
handling. Add the view command and complete the command summary.
Correct add and delete guidance, help output, and save behavior to
match the parser and model.

Use consistent contact terminology and remove guide references to
screenshots showing obsolete fields and an old help URL. Preserve
the actual data-file path so users can locate their saved contacts.

Refs #73, #74

commitResults.messageTitle: Add session undo history for contact changes
commitResults.messageBody:
Contact changes need a way to recover the previous state during a
session.

Keep up to 50 saved changes in memory and restore contacts, the
visible selection, and filter state with undo. Preserve later view
times without transferring them across reordered contacts.

Roll back failed saves and unexpected failures while leaving rejected
commands' visible list unchanged.

Fixes #108
